messages:
harper: quick idea for canaries — introduce a "traffic lens" that lets us route a tiny fingerprint of real traffic to the new variant while sending full requests to prod. goal: validate end-to-end without user-visible impact.

owen: can you expand on "fingerprint"? are we sampling headers, user-id hash, or full request shadow?

harper: minimal fingerprint — user_id_hash % 100000 + route + ephemeral nonce. lens test handler performs deterministic sampling and returns a short-circuit health probe to the variant; if probe is good, we promote sampling to full-body mirroring for that cohort.

nina: love the staged mirror. what happens when the variant starts returning partial failures after mirror promotion? we need a fast fallback that doesn't require global config churn.

harper: propose a local "soft-shear" at router level. it can apply a per-cohort weight that decays to 0 over <N> seconds when an error boundary is hit. soft-shear keeps session affinity for existing tokens to avoid user disruption.

kevin: we should define the error boundary carefully. example: 5xx spike > 1% in 30s OR p99 latency > 2s for the cohort. routers can apply a local backoff and report the event to controller.

owen: how do we keep autoscaler and cache layers aligned? if router reduces weight, cache warmness could be affected and autoscaler may scale down too quickly.

harper: introduce a "keep-warm" hint emitted by routers when soft-shear engages. hint: {route, cohort, ttl_seconds}. autoscaler and cache-controller subscribe to hints. autoscaler respects min_ttl before evict.

nina: API sketch for lens/controller please. also need signatures so we don't let any service flip cohorts.

harper: API sketch:

GET /lens/<route>/cohort -> {cohort_id, sample_rate, state}
POST /lens/claim -> {cohort_id, token, sample_result}
POST /soft-shear/event -> {cohort_id, cause, severity, router_id}
POST /hints/keep-warm -> {route, cohort, ttl}

kevin: prefer streaming updates over polling for sample_rate changes. use long-lived websocket/grpc stream and fall back to HTTP for one-offs.

infra-bot: note: rolling out streaming increases connection counts; we should bundle many routes per stream.

own: observability: emit these metrics per-cohort: lens.sampled_rps, lens.mirror_rps, lens.promoted_cohorts, soft_shear.active_cohorts, keeper.hints_emitted. also emit event traces for cohort lifecycle.

nina: policy language request: ops want to say "promote when error < 0.1% and p95 < 500ms for 10m, or rollback immediately on 5xx>0.5% for 30s". implement DSL or pluggable policy engine?

harper: pluggable engine recommended. controller ships with default policy set; teams can register a policy webhook that returns recommended actions. controller validates policy outputs and applies safe-guards (rate limits, escalation windows).

own: security: cohort tokens must be signed with controller key and include expiry + scope. routers validate signatures to avoid token replay.

kevin: testing note: need a traffic-replay harness that can replay production traces with user-id distribution so lens sampling fidelity is accurate. simulator can inject network faults and backpressure to tune decay timing.

nina: playbook idea: soft-shear event generates a "cohort incident" channel with quick checks: is token leaking? is cache hit ratio dropping? is autoscaler hint honored? add checklist steps.

harper: we should also allow a manual "freeze" that pins cohort state (no auto-promote) while SREs investigate. controller exposes freeze/unfreeze endpoints.

owen: implementation phasing: 1) lens sampling + streaming config 2) local soft-shear router logic + keep-warm hint 3) pluggable policy webhooks + simulator 4) playbooks/alerts.

kevin: one more: add a short 'cooldown blacklist' so cohorts that fail repeatedly aren't reopened for a configurable duration. prevents flip-flop.

ops-bot: infra:traffic-lens v0.1 -> deployed to canary :white_check_mark:

harper: I'll draft an RFC with API sketches, example policy DSL snippets, and simulator plan. can we meet Thurs?

own: Thurs morning works.

nina: I'll mock alert rules and a sample freeze flow.

kevin: I'll prototype the keep-warm hint consumer for autoscaler.

harper: thanks everyone :)
